title: Cantilene et Danse
identity: Denis Joly’s Cantilène et Danse is an eight-page Alphonse Leduc work for alto saxophone and piano (AL20698). The publisher describes slow cantabile and scherzando sections, later fast notes, trills, staccato, accidentals, and endurance demands. Scott D. Kallestad’s 2005 UNT DMA annotated bibliography treats it as a college-level candidate and appears on three college lists; the dissertation summary table labels it freshman.

evidence.claim: Publisher product page provides form, selected technique/demand notes, eight-page length and upper-intermediate label.
2026 CDMC Alsace repertoire list includes the title in an FC2 selection list.
Conservatoire de Lille lists it among reference works for its specialized-cycle saxophone entrance exam.

The UNT dissertation provides performance considerations: graceful slow-section lines, scales/arpeggios, fast sixteenths at dotted-quarter=120, a faster final segment, and a nine-measure optional cut; duration is reviewer-estimated 4:30. Its range notation uses the dissertation’s own octave designation chart.
evidence.source_name: Scott D. Kallestad, University of North Texas DMA dissertation (2005)

evidence.claim: The UNT dissertation’s selected-college repertoire appendix lists the work on three college/university lists; its summary table labels the work freshman. This aggregate label does not establish that each individual list assigned that rating.
evidence.source_name: Scott D. Kallestad, University of North Texas DMA dissertation (2005)

evidence.claim: The guide gives Andante cantabile quarter=88 and Allegro scherzando 6/8 at dotted-quarter=120.
evidence.source_name: Claude Delangle et al., 10 ans avec le saxophone (Philharmonie de Paris digital scan)

review_focus: Inference from the UNT performance analysis and the publisher’s notes: shape the cantabile phrases and manage fast scale/arpeggio sixteenths through the quicker close; inspect the score and decide whether the optional cut is appropriate.
collection_flag: Original alto saxophone and piano recital work. Two historically dated pedagogy sources discuss it, including a 2005 college-list survey; their grade/year systems differ and are not SaxoBrain levels.
gaps: Hal Leonard’s product description reports an upper-intermediate standard; CDMC uses its own FC2 scheme, which should not be mapped to SaxoBrain year.
No matching performance recording or visually inspected score preview found; UNT’s range uses its own octave chart and should not be copied into catalog fields without verification.
